exposure: Socioeconomic factors (rural residence, illiteracy, low socioeconomic status, caste, employment)
Pregnancy complications (anaemia, eclampsia, hypertensive disorders, haemorrhage, obstructed labour, breech presentation, abnormal fetal position)
finding: The study found a strong association between socioeconomic deprivation (rural residence, illiteracy, low socioeconomic status, schedule caste background, unemployment) and increased risk of stillbirth in India.
mod_finding: Assisted delivery and cesarean section were both associated with an increased odds of stillbirth.
